Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: logging controls / sensitive-data redaction

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps on the logging / PII redaction questions you raised: 

1) Scope of logs: you asked what we persist in request/response logs (headers, body, metadata, trace IDs). Short answer: by default Redwood captures metadata (timestamps, route/model, latency, request IDs, truncated token counts) but request/response bodies and headers are NOT persisted to long-term logs unless explicitly enabled. We provide configurable logging policies per customer (none, minimal metadata, full request/response).

2) Sensitive fields & redaction: we support rule-based redaction at ingestion (regex/key-based), model-output scrubbing, and automatic token-level masking for common PII types (SSNs, credit card patterns, emails). Redaction can be applied to both request payloads and response outputs before any logs are written.

3) Trace IDs & correlation headers: trace IDs are used for live debugging and short-term traces (retention default 7 days). You can opt into extended retention or disable storing full trace payloads; trace IDs remain in metadata for correlation but payloads can be excluded from persisted logs.

4) Data residency & retention: logs that include any customer content are kept in the region you select (US, EU, APAC). Retention is configurable (7, 30, 90, custom) and we can commit to deletion policies for enterprise contracts.

Next steps I recommend:
- I attached a short PDF that summarizes our redaction options and the default behaviors (redwood-logging-redaction-options.pdf).
- Dev (cc'd) can follow up with a quick tech note on how rule-based redaction is configured in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- If helpful, we can set up a 30-min follow-up with your security team to walk through a sample ingestion flow and retention controls.

Action items: 
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether you require request/response bodies to be persisted to long-term logs or if metadata-only retention is acceptable.
- Marissa (me) / Dev: prepare a scoped SOW language for retention & deletion for legal review if they need contractual commitments.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- For PCI/PII concerns, we cannot persist full request/response bodies to long-term logs. Metadata-only is our preferred default. If certain fields must be retained for debugging we need explicit field-level redaction or tokenization.
- Trace IDs: keeping trace IDs and minimal metadata for 30 days is acceptable, but the full trace payloads must be removed unless we explicitly enable them for a troubleshooting window (1-3 days) with audit logs.
- Retention: 30 days metadata-only for production is our starting point; we may want 90 days for non-production.

Could Dev share a short example config snippet showing how we would redact headers (e.g., Authorization / X-Forwarded-For) and mask response tokens? That will help our security team evaluate implementation risk.

Also: can you attach SOC 2 Type II summary or a link to your security package? Priya will coordinate legal review.

Appreciate it — we’re close on technical fit and this will move fast once we lock those items.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, FintechCo

Alex —

Thanks — quick technical examples below to illustrate options. I will drop these into the shared Drive folder and we can iterate.

1) Example rule-based redaction (ingestion pipeline):
- rule: redact header Authorization and X-Forwarded-For
- rule: redact JSON keys matching /.*(ssn|card_number|email).*/i
- rule action: replace value with <REDACTED:PII>

2) Masking model outputs: token-level post-process strip for regex matches (credit card patterns, SSN). We also support custom allowlists and denylists for entities.

3) Trace retention policy example:
- metadata-only retention: 30 days (default for prod)
- full trace payload: disabled unless enabled by a scoped support ticket (enabled window: 48 hours, logged to audit stream)

Attached is a short tech note and a sample JSON config. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min tech session where I walk through the policy UI and a live demo in a sandbox.

Cheers,
